neighbours.label: future passive notification in service / event information: 'you will be advised/notified', 'signs will be posted', 'we will let you know'
fire: Delivery times vary, and you will be informed by text once your parcel is on its way.
Full timetables for the replacement buses will be published on our website next week.
If your flight is changed, the airline will contact you with the new details.
Successful applicants will be notified by email within ten working days.
Parking arrangements for the festival will be announced closer to the date.
Any extra charges will be explained to you before the work begins.
Our customer team will get back to you as soon as the item is back in stock.
Room allocations will be emailed to all guests the week before arrival.
quiet: Delivery was slow, and I was informed by a neighbour that my parcel had arrived.
The timetables for the old buses were published in the local paper in 1982.
When my flight was changed, I contacted the airline and complained loudly.
The successful applicants were celebrating in the pub after the results came out.
The parking at last year's festival was a muddy field behind the stage.
The extra charges surprised him, and he argued with the builder for an hour.
Our customer team spent the afternoon restocking the shelves in the shop.
The guests chose their own rooms when they arrived at the old farmhouse.

notes: Card: ' advised' x2, ' posted' x3, ' will' x4, ' know' x2 in shop/event notices. Probe: 'will be posted' 0.70, 'will let you know' 0.50, past-tense 'was advised'/'posted the letter' near zero. Near misses keep the same verbs in past or non-notice use.
